title: The water cycle
notes: Sun, ocean, mountains, a river and clouds. Arrows only: two wavy arrows up from the ocean (evaporation), a curved arrow from the white cloud to the rain cloud (condensation and cloud movement), a down arrow in the rain (precipitation), and an arrow along the land to the ocean (runoff and collection).

title: Weather map with fronts
notes: Simplified contiguous U.S. outline. Red L in the Plains with a cold front (blue, triangles pointing east/southeast, the way it moves) running southwest and a warm front (red, half-circles pointing north) running east, which becomes a stationary front (alternating blue triangles on the south side and red half-circles on the north side). Blue H in the West. Green rain area with raindrops near the low and along the fronts. Only letters H and L.

title: Plate boundaries
notes: Three panels, left to right. Divergent: cross-section of a mid-ocean ridge, plates moving apart, magma rising in the gap, mantle currents rising in the middle. Convergent: oceanic plate sinking (subducting) under a continental plate at a trench, magma rising to a volcano. Transform: two blocks seen from above sliding past each other, with a stream and a road offset along the fault. No words.

title: World map of the continents
notes: Seven continents in flat colors on a Robinson projection, no labels: North America orange (with Greenland), South America green, Europe purple, Africa yellow, Asia red, Oceania tan, Antarctica white. Coastlines are computed from Natural Earth 1:110m country outlines (public-domain map data, used as coordinates only) and simplified; Russia is split into Europe and Asia at 60°E (standing in for the Urals). Layout and colors-by-continent were checked against a Wikimedia Commons continents map, used only as a visual reference.

title: The Sun
use: Sun picture (stars, the Sun as a star)
notes: Yellow-orange disk, darker toward the edge, with two sunspot pairs and one single spot, a soft glow around it and one prominence loop at the edge; dark space. No face.

title: Phases of the Moon
notes: Eight phases in reading order, two rows: new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous; full, waning gibbous, third quarter, waning crescent. Northern Hemisphere view: waxing phases lit on the right, waning phases lit on the left. Gray arrows between phases in each row. Dark sky with a few stars; no words.

title: Earth from space
notes: Globe centered near 12° N, 72° W: North and South America, Greenland (white ice), the edge of Africa and Europe, a sliver of Antarctica. Cloud bands, a hurricane in the Atlantic, thin blue atmosphere glow, night-side shading, a few stars on black.
